## Zoom Level Computation Strategy

Based on PERFORMANCE_ANALYSIS.md and standard web mapping:

**Goal:** Pre-compute markers at each zoom level (0-18) instead of storing everything at zoom=0

**Approach:**
- **Zoom ≥8:** Keep all individual markers (full detail)
- **Zoom <8:** Cluster markers into grid cells, create aggregated representative markers
- Use **deterministic spatial grid** (not random sampling)
- Preserve important markers (high radiation, has spectrum)

Let me create the implementation:

input.content:
-- Migration: Pre-compute zoom levels for performance optimization
--
-- PROBLEM: All 133M markers stored at zoom=0 causes slow queries
-- SOLUTION: Pre-compute appropriate zoom levels for each marker
--
-- Strategy:
-- - Zoom ≥8: Store all individual markers (full detail)
-- - Zoom <8: Cluster markers into spatial grid cells
-- - Use deterministic grid-based clustering (not random sampling)
-- - Aggregate values: average dose rate, count, etc.
--
-- This will reduce query result sets from millions to thousands of rows

-- ============================================
-- PHASE 1: Assign zoom levels to existing markers
-- ============================================

-- For zoom levels 8-18: All markers should be visible individually
-- We'll update markers to have their natural zoom level based on detail level
-- For now, we'll compute based on track density or use zoom=10 as default for imported data

-- Calculate appropriate zoom level for each marker based on spatial density
-- Higher density areas = higher zoom level needed to distinguish markers
-- Lower density = visible at lower zoom levels

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION calculate_marker_zoom(lat DOUBLE PRECISION, lon DOUBLE PRECISION, trackid VARCHAR)
RETURNS INTEGER AS $$
DECLARE
    marker_count INTEGER;
    zoom_level INTEGER;
    grid_size DOUBLE PRECISION;
BEGIN
    -- Default zoom level for individual markers
    zoom_level := 10;

    -- Check density in 1km grid cell (roughly zoom 13)
    grid_size := 0.01; -- ~1km at equator

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO marker_count
    FROM markers m
    WHERE m.lat BETWEEN lat - grid_size AND lat + grid_size
      AND m.lon BETWEEN lon - grid_size AND lon + grid_size
      AND m.trackid = trackid
    LIMIT 1000; -- Avoid counting huge numbers

    -- Assign zoom based on density
    IF marker_count > 500 THEN
        zoom_level := 15;  -- Very dense, need high zoom
    ELSIF marker_count > 100 THEN
        zoom_level := 13;  -- Dense area
    ELSIF marker_count > 20 THEN
        zoom_level := 11;  -- Medium density
    ELSE
        zoom_level := 10;  -- Low density
    END IF;

    RETURN zoom_level;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- ============================================
-- PHASE 2: Create aggregated markers for lower zoom levels
-- ============================================

-- Create a function to generate grid-based clustered markers for a specific zoom level
-- This uses a spatial grid to deterministically cluster markers

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION create_zoom_level_markers(target_zoom INTEGER)
RETURNS VOID AS $$
DECLARE
    grid_degrees DOUBLE PRECISION;
    inserted_count INTEGER;
BEGIN
    -- Calculate grid size in degrees for this zoom level
    -- Zoom 0: ~40,000 km (whole world) = ~360 degrees
    -- Zoom 1: ~20,000 km = ~180 degrees
    -- Zoom 5: ~1,250 km = ~11.25 degrees
    -- Zoom 7: ~312 km = ~2.8 degrees

    grid_degrees := 360.0 / POWER(2, target_zoom + 1);

    RAISE NOTICE 'Creating zoom level % markers with grid size % degrees', target_zoom, grid_degrees;

    -- Insert aggregated markers for this zoom level
    -- Group by grid cell, aggregate values
    INSERT INTO markers (
        doseRate,
        date,
        lon,
        lat,
        countRate,
        zoom,
        speed,
        trackID,
        geom,
        has_spectrum,
        marker_count  -- Store how many original markers this represents
    )
    SELECT
        AVG(doseRate) as doseRate,                        -- Average dose rate in cell
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY date) as date,  -- Median date
        (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lon,    -- Grid cell center
        (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lat,    -- Grid cell center
        AVG(countRate) as countRate,                      -- Average count rate
        target_zoom as zoom,                              -- Target zoom level
        AVG(speed) as speed,                              -- Average speed
        'cluster_' || target_zoom || '_' ||
            FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees)::TEXT || '_' ||
            FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees)::TEXT as trackID,   -- Unique cluster ID
        ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(
            (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees,
            (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees
        ), 4326) as geom,
        BOOL_OR(has_spectrum) as has_spectrum,            -- True if any marker has spectrum
        COUNT(*)::INTEGER as marker_count                 -- Count of markers in cluster
    FROM markers
    WHERE zoom = 0  -- Source from original zoom=0 markers
    GROUP BY
        FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees),
        FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees)
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 0;

    GET DIAGNOSTICS inserted_count = ROW_COUNT;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Inserted % aggregated markers for zoom level %', inserted_count, target_zoom;

END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- ============================================
-- PHASE 3: Add marker_count column to track aggregated markers
-- ============================================

-- Add column to store how many original markers an aggregated marker represents
ALTER TABLE markers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS marker_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1;

-- Update existing markers to have marker_count = 1 (individual markers)
UPDATE markers SET marker_count = 1 WHERE marker_count IS NULL;

-- ============================================
-- EXECUTION PLAN (Run these manually in order)
-- ============================================

-- STEP 1: Create zoom levels 7, 5, 3, 1 (working from high to low zoom)
-- Start with higher zooms first as they have more detail

-- SELECT create_zoom_level_markers(7);  -- ~2.8 degree grid (~312 km)
-- SELECT create_zoom_level_markers(5);  -- ~11.25 degree grid (~1,250 km)
-- SELECT create_zoom_level_markers(3);  -- ~45 degree grid (~5,000 km)
-- SELECT create_zoom_level_markers(1);  -- ~180 degree grid (~20,000 km)

-- STEP 2: Verify results
-- SELECT zoom, COUNT(*),
--        AVG(marker_count) as avg_markers_per_cluster,
--        SUM(marker_count) as total_markers_represented
-- FROM markers
-- GROUP BY zoom
-- ORDER BY zoom;

-- STEP 3: Create indexes for new zoom levels
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_markers_geom_gist ON markers USING GIST(geom) WHERE zoom > 0;
-- ANALYZE markers;

-- STEP 4: Update application to query appropriate zoom level instead of always zoom=0
-- (This requires code changes in Go application)

COMMENT ON FUNCTION create_zoom_level_markers IS
'Creates aggregated markers for a specific zoom level using deterministic grid-based clustering';

COMMENT ON FUNCTION calculate_marker_zoom IS
'Calculates appropriate zoom level for a marker based on spatial density';

-- Populate pre-computed zoom levels in batches
-- This migration creates aggregated markers for zoom levels 7-10
-- Run time: ~30-60 minutes for 133M markers

-- ============================================
-- SETUP: Add marker_count column
-- ============================================

ALTER TABLE markers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS marker_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_markers_marker_count ON markers(marker_count) WHERE marker_count > 1;

-- ============================================
-- FUNCTION: Create zoom level in batches
-- ============================================

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION populate_zoom_level_batch(
    target_zoom INTEGER,
    batch_size INTEGER DEFAULT 10000000
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    batch_num INTEGER,
    clusters_created INTEGER,
    markers_processed INTEGER
) AS $$
DECLARE
    grid_degrees DOUBLE PRECISION;
    total_markers BIGINT;
    offset_val BIGINT := 0;
    batch_count INTEGER := 0;
    clusters_in_batch INTEGER;
BEGIN
    -- Calculate grid size for this zoom level
    grid_degrees := 360.0 / POWER(2, target_zoom + 1);

    -- Get total markers to process
    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO total_markers FROM markers WHERE zoom = 0;

    RAISE NOTICE 'Zoom %: Creating clusters with %.3f degree grid (%.1f km)',
        target_zoom, grid_degrees, grid_degrees * 111;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Processing % markers in batches of %', total_markers, batch_size;

    -- Process in batches
    LOOP
        batch_count := batch_count + 1;

        -- Create aggregated markers for this batch
        WITH batch_markers AS (
            SELECT *
            FROM markers
            WHERE zoom = 0
            ORDER BY id
            LIMIT batch_size OFFSET offset_val
        )
        INSERT INTO markers (
            doseRate,
            date,
            lon,
            lat,
            countRate,
            zoom,
            speed,
            trackID,
            geom,
            has_spectrum,
            marker_count,
            temperature,
            humidity
        )
        SELECT
            AVG(doseRate) as doseRate,
            PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY date)::BIGINT as date,
            (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lon,
            (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lat,
            AVG(countRate) as countRate,
            target_zoom as zoom,
            AVG(COALESCE(speed, 0)) as speed,
            'z' || target_zoom || '_' ||
                FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees)::TEXT || '_' ||
                FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees)::TEXT as trackID,
            ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(
                (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees,
                (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees
            ), 4326) as geom,
            BOOL_OR(COALESCE(has_spectrum, FALSE)) as has_spectrum,
            COUNT(*)::INTEGER as marker_count,
            AVG(COALESCE(temperature, 0)) as temperature,
            AVG(COALESCE(humidity, 0)) as humidity
        FROM batch_markers
        GROUP BY
            FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees),
            FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees)
        ON CONFLICT (trackid, date, lat, lon) DO UPDATE
            SET marker_count = markers.marker_count + EXCLUDED.marker_count,
                doseRate = (markers.doseRate * markers.marker_count + EXCLUDED.doseRate * EXCLUDED.marker_count) /
                          (markers.marker_count + EXCLUDED.marker_count);

        GET DIAGNOSTICS clusters_in_batch = ROW_COUNT;

        RAISE NOTICE 'Batch %: Created % clusters from % markers (offset: %)',
            batch_count, clusters_in_batch, LEAST(batch_size, total_markers - offset_val), offset_val;

        -- Return progress
        batch_num := batch_count;
        clusters_created := clusters_in_batch;
        markers_processed := LEAST(batch_size, total_markers - offset_val);
        RETURN NEXT;

        offset_val := offset_val + batch_size;

        -- Exit if we've processed all markers
        EXIT WHEN offset_val >= total_markers;

        -- Checkpoint every 5 batches
        IF batch_count % 5 = 0 THEN
            RAISE NOTICE 'Checkpoint: % of % markers processed (%.1f%%)',
                offset_val, total_markers, 100.0 * offset_val / total_markers;
        END IF;
    END LOOP;

    RAISE NOTICE 'Completed zoom %: % batches processed', target_zoom, batch_count;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- ============================================
-- EXECUTION INSTRUCTIONS
-- ============================================

/*
 * Run these commands in order (each takes ~15-20 minutes):
 *
 * -- Create zoom 10 (most useful - 20km grid)
 * SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(10, 5000000);
 * ANALYZE markers;
 *
 * -- Create zoom 9 (39km grid)
 * SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(9, 10000000);
 * ANALYZE markers;
 *
 * -- Create zoom 8 (78km grid)
 * SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(8, 10000000);
 * ANALYZE markers;
 *
 * -- Create zoom 7 (156km grid)
 * SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(7, 10000000);
 * ANALYZE markers;
 *
 * -- Check results:
 * SELECT zoom,
 *        COUNT(*) as clusters,
 *        AVG(marker_count) as avg_markers_per_cluster,
 *        SUM(marker_count) as total_represented,
 *        pg_size_pretty(SUM(pg_column_size(geom))) as geom_size
 * FROM markers
 * WHERE zoom > 0
 * GROUP BY zoom
 * ORDER BY zoom;
 *
 * -- Total time: ~60-90 minutes for all zoom levels
 * -- Disk space: ~2-3GB additional (small compared to existing 133M markers)
 */

# Performance Issue Root Cause & Solution

## What We Discovered Today

### ❌ The Attempted Fix That FAILED:
1. Created composite GIST index `idx_markers_zoom_geom_gist` on `(zoom, geom)`
2. **This index was INVALID** (`indisvalid = false`)
3. PostgreSQL refused to use it → fell back to seq scans
4. Made performance **WORSE** locally (10x+ slower)
5. **Never deployed to production** (production doesn't have this broken index)

### ✅ The Real Problem:
- **ALL 133M markers stored at zoom=0**
- Query: `WHERE zoom = 0 AND geom && bbox`
- Even with perfect index, filtering `zoom=0` selects 100% of data
- PostgreSQL correctly chooses seq scan when selecting most of table
- Result: **7-8 second TTFB**

### 🎯 The Real Solution: Pre-computed Zoom Levels

**Not** better indexes, but **pre-compute appropriate zoom levels**!

## Current Status

### ✅ Completed:
1. **Restored working index locally**: Dropped invalid composite index, recreated `idx_markers_geom_gist`
2. **Analyzed zoom level requirements**: Tested different grid sizes to find optimal clustering
3. **Created migration scripts**:
   - [`compute_zoom_levels.sql`](migrations/compute_zoom_levels.sql) - Functions for zoom computation
   - [`populate_zoom_levels_batch.sql`](migrations/populate_zoom_levels_batch.sql) - Batch processing for production
   - [`test_zoom_computation.sql`](migrations/test_zoom_computation.sql) - Testing script
4. **Documented code changes**: [`ZOOM_LEVEL_CODE_CHANGES.md`](ZOOM_LEVEL_CODE_CHANGES.md)

### ⚠️ Production Status:
- **Production is still slow** (7-8 second TTFB)
- **Production does NOT have the broken composite index** (good!)
- **Production needs** the zoom level solution implemented

## The Solution in 3 Steps

### Step 1: Populate Zoom Levels (Database)
Run on production PostgreSQL (~60-90 minutes total):

```sql
-- Add marker_count column
ALTER TABLE markers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS marker_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1;

-- Load the function
\i migrations/populate_zoom_levels_batch.sql

-- Create zoom 10 (~20km grid) - most useful
SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(10, 5000000);
ANALYZE markers;

-- Create zoom 9 (~39km grid)
SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(9, 10000000);
ANALYZE markers;

-- Create zoom 8 (~78km grid)
SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(8, 10000000);
ANALYZE markers;

-- Create zoom 7 (~156km grid)
SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_level_batch(7, 10000000);
ANALYZE markers;

-- Verify results:
SELECT zoom,
       COUNT(*) as clusters,
       AVG(marker_count) as avg_markers_per_cluster,
       pg_size_pretty(SUM(pg_column_size(geom))) as size
FROM markers
WHERE zoom > 0
GROUP BY zoom
ORDER BY zoom;
```

**Expected result:**
| Zoom | Clusters | Avg Markers/Cluster | Size |
|------|----------|---------------------|------|
| 7 | ~50-100 | ~1-2M | ~500KB |
| 8 | ~200-500 | ~300k | ~2MB |
| 9 | ~1k-2k | ~80k | ~10MB |
| 10 | ~5k-10k | ~15k | ~50MB |

### Step 2: Update Go Code
Apply changes from [`ZOOM_LEVEL_CODE_CHANGES.md`](ZOOM_LEVEL_CODE_CHANGES.md):

1. Add `mapClientZoomToDBZoom()` function
2. Replace `const rawZoom = 0` with client zoom mapping (2 locations)
3. Update map.html to pass zoom parameter in API calls

**Key change:**
```go
// BEFORE
const rawZoom = 0

// AFTER
clientZoom := getClientZoom(r)  // From query param
dbZoom := mapClientZoomToDBZoom(clientZoom)  // Map to DB zoom
```

### Step 3: Deploy
```bash
# Build
go build -o safecast-new-map .

# Deploy to production (FOLLOW EXACT ORDER from MEMORY.md)
ssh root@simplemap.safecast.org "systemctl stop safecast-new-map"
rsync -avP ./safecast-new-map root@simplemap.safecast.org:/usr/local/bin/
ssh root@simplemap.safecast.org "systemctl start safecast-new-map"
ssh root@simplemap.safecast.org "systemctl status safecast-new-map"
```

## Expected Performance Improvement

### Tokyo Example (7M markers):

| Scenario | DB Zoom | Rows Scanned | Time | Improvement |
|----------|---------|--------------|------|-------------|
| **Before** | 0 (all) | 7,000,000 | 7800ms | baseline |
| **After (zoom 7)** | 7 | 4 | 50ms | **156x faster** |
| **After (zoom 10)** | 9 | 16 | 80ms | **97x faster** |
| **After (zoom 12)** | 10 | 42 | 100ms | **78x faster** |

**Overall: 50-100x performance improvement**

## Risk Assessment

### Low Risk:
- ✅ Zoom=0 markers remain unchanged (backward compatible)
- ✅ Can rollback code changes easily
- ✅ New zoom level markers are additive (don't break existing functionality)
- ✅ Migration runs in batches (non-blocking)

### Potential Issues:
- ⚠️ Disk space: +2-3GB for new zoom level markers (~2% increase)
- ⚠️ Migration time: ~60-90 minutes (run during low-traffic period)
- ⚠️ Need to update import pipeline to compute zooms for new data (future work)

## Testing Checklist

### Before Production:
- [ ] Test locally with sample zoom levels
- [ ] Verify queries use correct zoom level
- [ ] Check performance with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
- [ ] Test at different zoom levels (0-18)
- [ ] Verify marker_count aggregation is correct

### After Production Deploy:
- [ ] Monitor query times (should drop from 7-8s to 50-100ms)
- [ ] Check database size increase
- [ ] Verify map displays correctly at all zoom levels
- [ ] Monitor error logs for any issues

## Next Steps

1. **Immediate (Today):**
   - Test solution locally on development database
   - Verify performance improvements
   - Review code changes

2. **Short-term (This Week):**
   - Run migration on production (low-traffic time)
   - Deploy code changes
   - Monitor performance

3. **Long-term (This Month):**
   - Update import pipeline to compute zooms for new uploads
   - Consider creating additional zoom levels (11-18) for full detail
   - Add monitoring for query performance metrics

## Files Created

1. `migrations/compute_zoom_levels.sql` - Core zoom computation functions
2. `migrations/populate_zoom_levels_batch.sql` - Production batch migration
3. `migrations/test_zoom_computation.sql` - Testing queries
4. `ZOOM_LEVEL_CODE_CHANGES.md` - Go code changes needed
5. `SOLUTION_SUMMARY.md` - This file

## Questions?

- **Why not just use better indexes?** Because 100% of data is zoom=0. No index helps when you're selecting everything.
- **Why these specific zoom levels?** Based on analysis: zoom 7-10 gives optimal clustering (4 to ~500 clusters vs millions)
- **What about data after zoom 10?** Client-side clustering still works, but now on hundreds of markers instead of millions
- **Can we delete zoom=0 markers?** No! They're the source of truth. Zoom 7-10 are aggregated views.
- **What if import adds new data?** New imports still go to zoom=0. We'll need to update import pipeline later.

---

**Summary: We need pre-computed zoom levels, not better indexes. The solution is ready to implement.**

-- Simplified zoom level population (no ON CONFLICT)
-- Run time: ~15-20 minutes per zoom level

-- Add marker_count column if not exists
ALTER TABLE markers ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS marker_count INTEGER DEFAULT 1;

-- Simple function to populate one zoom level at a time
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION populate_zoom_simple(target_zoom INTEGER)
RETURNS TABLE (clusters_created BIGINT) AS $$
DECLARE
    grid_degrees DOUBLE PRECISION;
    rows_inserted BIGINT;
BEGIN
    -- Calculate grid size for this zoom level
    grid_degrees := 360.0 / POWER(2, target_zoom + 1);

    RAISE NOTICE 'Creating zoom % clusters with %.3f degree grid (%.1f km)',
        target_zoom, grid_degrees, grid_degrees * 111;

    -- Insert aggregated markers for this zoom level
    INSERT INTO markers (
        doseRate,
        date,
        lon,
        lat,
        countRate,
        zoom,
        speed,
        trackID,
        geom,
        has_spectrum,
        marker_count,
        temperature,
        humidity
    )
    SELECT
        AVG(doseRate) as doseRate,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY date)::BIGINT as date,
        (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lon,
        (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees as lat,
        AVG(countRate) as countRate,
        target_zoom as zoom,
        AVG(COALESCE(speed, 0)) as speed,
        'z' || target_zoom || '_' ||
            FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees)::TEXT || '_' ||
            FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees)::TEXT as trackID,
        ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(
            (FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees,
            (FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees) + 0.5) * grid_degrees
        ), 4326) as geom,
        BOOL_OR(COALESCE(has_spectrum, FALSE)) as has_spectrum,
        COUNT(*)::INTEGER as marker_count,
        AVG(COALESCE(temperature, 0)) as temperature,
        AVG(COALESCE(humidity, 0)) as humidity
    FROM markers
    WHERE zoom = 0  -- Source from original zoom=0 markers
    GROUP BY
        FLOOR(lon / grid_degrees),
        FLOOR(lat / grid_degrees);

    GET DIAGNOSTICS rows_inserted = ROW_COUNT;
    RAISE NOTICE 'Created % clusters for zoom level %', rows_inserted, target_zoom;

    clusters_created := rows_inserted;
    RETURN NEXT;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Usage:
-- SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_simple(10);
-- SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_simple(9);
-- SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_simple(8);
-- SELECT * FROM populate_zoom_simple(7);

// mapClientZoomToDBZoom maps client zoom to database zoom for hybrid strategy.
//
// Strategy:
//   - Client zoom 0-10: Use pre-computed cluster zoom levels (1-10)
//   - Client zoom 11+: Use zoom=0 (original markers, fast via spatial index)
//
// At high zoom (11+), viewport is small (~1-10 km²), so even though we query
// zoom=0 (133M markers), the spatial index efficiently filters to just the
// thousands of markers in the small viewport. This is FAST.
//
// At low zoom (1-10), viewport is huge (continents/countries), so we MUST use
// pre-computed clusters to avoid scanning millions of markers.
func mapClientZoomToDBZoom(clientZoom int) int {
	// High zoom (street/building level): use original zoom=0 markers
	// Spatial filter on small viewport is fast even with 133M markers
	if clientZoom >= 11 {
		return 0
	}

	// Low zoom (continent/country/region): use pre-computed clusters
	// Direct mapping: client zoom = db zoom (1-10)
	if clientZoom < 1 {
		return 1  // Minimum cluster zoom
	}

	return clientZoom  // 1-10: use corresponding cluster zoom level
}
